description: Resolves a traveler input reference (traveler_id::input_name) so the NCR initiation form can show the traveler's title and the input's label before the user submits (spec FR-004). Read-only; creates nothing. Must be registered before router.get('/:id') in routes/ncr.js so 'traveler-input' is not treated as an NCR id. Uses exactly the same resolver as POST /api/ncrs, so the preview can never disagree with what submission will accept.
authorization: The caller must have at least read access to the referenced traveler (reqUtils.canRead). A caller without it receives the SAME response as for a nonexistent traveler, so a traveler's existence, title and input labels are never disclosed (spec FR-008).

ref.description: The reference, format traveler_id::input_name. Leading/trailing whitespace ignored; split at the first '::'; at most 256 characters after trimming.

traveler.title: string
traveler.status: number — 1 (only an active traveler resolves successfully)

input.name: string — key of the traveler's active-form labels
input.label: string — the human-readable label the NCR will record

bad_reference_400.when: missing/blank ref, longer than 256 characters, no '::', empty traveler id or input name, or a traveler id that is not a valid ObjectId

traveler_not_found_404.when: no such traveler, OR the caller lacks read access to it (deliberately identical)

input_not_found_404.when: the traveler exists and the caller can read it, but the input name is not in its active form's labels. Only returned after the read-access check passes.

body.message: Traveler "<title>" is <status_label>; an NCR can only be initiated against an active traveler.

traveler_not_active_409.when: the traveler is readable and the input exists, but Traveler.status !== 1. status_label comes from model/traveler.js statusMap (e.g. 'submitted for completion').

notes: Check order is fixed: parse -> ObjectId validity -> load -> read access -> input exists -> active. See data-model.md.
The same error body shape as POST /api/ncrs (success/error/message/details), so views/ncr-create.jade's existing renderer handles it.
The client debounces (~300 ms) and calls this on input and blur. It never blocks submit: the server re-resolves on POST (spec FR-007).
